jobs.title: Agriculture Education Manager at Greenacres Foundation
jobs.description: Employer: Greenacres Foundation Expires: 08/27/2026 Greenacres Foundation (GAF): Greenacres Foundation offers a variety of experiences for everyone. Our campuses are living classrooms, where programming can explore the natural environment, horsemanship, the arts, and generative agriculture. Whether it's an educational field trip, fun summer camps, farm-fresh products or events which blend learning and celebration, a quality experience awaits every guest. Our team at Greenacres is passionate and dedicated to our Mission and brings inspiration to all our endeavors. Our unwavering commitment shines through in how we embrace our operating values - Grace, Generative, Giving, Good Neighbor Policy, and Green. Our team always aims for excellence, prioritizing Quality, Quality, Quality (QQQ) in every endeavor. We thrive in a collaborative environment where teamwork leads to achievements. More than a workplace, Greenacres is a career, a lifestyle and a place to wholeheartedly embrace the Mission and Values set forth by our visionary Founders, Louis and Louise Nippert. Here, dedication isn't just a requirement; it's a way of life. Summary: The Agriculture Education Manager is deeply committed to the mission and values of Greenacres. As Agriculture Education Manager, you’ll shape how thousands of students experience agriculture. Leading educators and teaching children how to connect learning to real land, animals, and food systems. This role is responsible for leading a team of four Agriculture and Equine Education Site Supervisors, supporting expansion to new sites as they arise, and overseeing the development and implementation of agriculture-based curriculum. The Agriculture Education Manager also plays a key role in onboarding, supporting, and leading education staff within the Agriculture Education department. The ability to build a strong culture, unify a newer team, and coach for excellence in the informal education space is critical for the team. A strong and consistent communicator is a best fit for this role. This position reports to the Senior Director of Education and works collaboratively and communicates effectively with other Education Managers, Education Operations, as well as the Livestock, Equine, and Garden teams, to ensure all programming reflects Greenacres’ mission and values and fosters a culture of transparency, honesty, and integrity. Responsibilities: Responsibilities of the Agriculture Education Manager include: Education Programs Hire, supervise, train, evaluate, and develop Agriculture Education Site Supervisors and educators Lead and support the development and implementation of educational plans for current and future program sites Conduct ongoing program evaluation and implement improvements as needed Maintain accurate agriculture education program logs and programming records Serve as a substitute educator at all four Agriculture and Equine Education sites as needed Communicate effectively across locations and between GAF departments to problem-solve and innovate Staff Management Lead and facilitate regular team meetings Hold Site Supervisors accountable for staff management, program quality, and program development Complete administrative and reporting duties as required Coach and develop Site Supervisors’ leadership and management skills Collaborate with departments across GAF to build partnerships, align priorities, and achieve shared organizational goals Budget Partner with Site Supervisors to prepare and propose annual programming budgets for each site to the Senior Director of Education and CFO Monitor and review monthly actuals versus budget, identifying trends and addressing variances Additional Professional Activities Support the professional development of Agriculture and Equine Education staff, collaborating with Livestock, Garden, and Equine teams on cross-functional opportunities Attend events to represent Greenacres through presentations to public and community groups Communicate and coordinate effectively with the Livestock, Equine, and Garden teams to ensure high-quality, mission-aligned programming, and provide operational support as appropriate RequirementsBachelor’s degree in education or comparable academic discipline or equivalent experientially gained knowledge. 4+ years proven management/supervisory experience. 6+ years of demonstrable education and agriculture, or related, experience preferred. Passion for educating school-age children utilizing authentic agriculture assets. Strong knowledge, skill, and experience in livestock, equine, and/or garden production with sustainable methods. Knowledge of regenerative agriculture through holistic management farm practices. Proven ability to initiate, organize and implement plans. High attention to detail and excellent judgment. Excellent interpersonal skills; strong oral and written communication skills. Ability to handle confidential information. Ability to perform essential job functions, including lifting up to 50 pounds and prolonged standing, walking, sitting, and working in varied indoor and outdoor environments, with or without reasonable accommodation. Willingness and ability to travel to multiple Greenacres sites and campuses, which currently include Indian Hill, OH, Oldenburg, IN, Miami Township Clermont Co., and Felicity, OH. Contribute to a strong organizational culture by supporting teammates, encouraging collaboration, and promoting a positive workplace environment. Ability to manage and lead a team of dedicated agriculture educators to assure QQQ and our values of Grace, Good Neighbor Policy and Green. Ability to successfully pass a post-offer pre-employment drug test and fingerprint FBI background screen. Why Choose Us?As a company, we invest in our employees in all aspects of their life. We believe that the health and welfare of yourself and your family are very important. Listed below, you will find some of our top benefits and perks. Market Competitive Salary Generous PTO Package 10 Paid Holidays Paid Family Medical Leave Comprehensive Medical, Dental, Vision and Life Insurance Plans Employer funded Simplified Employee Pension Plan Short and Long Term Disability Insurance Fun & Engaging Culture Ongoing training, education, and industry partnerships that allow you to be up to speed on the latest innovations, technologies and processes. Greenacres Foundation is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business need.

jobs.description: Employer: Bard Early Colleges / Bard High School Early College (Headquarters) Expires: 08/27/2026 Full-time Faculty - Studio and Visual Arts Apply Using This Link: https://apply.interfolio.com/147150Bard High School Early College Brooklyn, a partnership between Bard College and the New York City Department of Education, invites applications for a faculty member in Studio and Visual Arts to join our faculty for the campus’ 2026-2027 academic year. The Bard Early Colleges (BEC) are founded on the belief that, for many young people, college can and should start at an earlier age. Acting on this belief, Bard Early College enables students to begin serious college study in place of the traditional 11th and 12th grades, at no cost to students or families. The Bard Early Colleges offer a unique home for young people’s intellectual ambition: as both tuition-free, branch campuses of Bard College and public high schools, they award a high school diploma and a Bard College Associate in Arts degree (and 60 transferable credits) by the end of the 12th grade. Students are taught by Bard College faculty in undergraduate seminar classes, all deeply rooted in the liberal arts and sciences, in Bard College’s commitment to excellence in teaching, and in Bard’s mission as a private college in the public interest. Now entering its third decade, the Bard Early College network enrolls over 3,300 young people in campuses in Queens, Manhattan, the Bronx, Brooklyn, and Hudson, New York; Newark, New Jersey; New Orleans, Louisiana; Cleveland, Ohio; Baltimore, Maryland; and Washington, D.C. Position DutiesBHSEC Brooklyn seeks candidates able to teach a broad range of courses in studio and visual arts; ability to cover multiple fields is especially desirable. Candidates will teach courses in their field of specialization, as well as survey courses in the theory, history, appreciation and criticism of the fine arts. Successful applicants will be able to develop and implement innovative and engaging lesson plans that foster creativity and artistic expression, using a variety of teaching methods to meet the needs of diverse learners. Successful candidates will foster an appreciation of the cultural and historical contexts of studio and visual arts, emphasizing the diverse perspectives and experiences of artists from different cultures and time periods. jobs.description: Employer: Bard Early Colleges / Bard High School Early College (Headquarters) Expires: 08/27/2026 Full-time Faculty - Literature of the AmericasApply Here: https://apply.interfolio.com/170074Bard High School Early College Brooklyn, a partnership between Bard College and the New York City Department of Education, invites applications for a faculty member in Literature of the Americas to join our faculty for the campus’ 2026-2027 academic year. The Bard Early Colleges (BEC) are founded on the belief that, for many young people, college can and should start at an earlier age. Acting on this belief, Bard Early College enables students to begin serious college study in place of the traditional 11th and 12th grades, at no cost to students or families. The Bard Early Colleges offer a unique home for young people’s intellectual ambition: as both tuition-free, branch campuses of Bard College and public high schools, they award a high school diploma and a Bard College Associate in Arts degree (and 60 transferable credits) by the end of the 12th grade. Students are taught by Bard College faculty in undergraduate seminar classes, all deeply rooted in the liberal arts and sciences, in Bard College’s commitment to excellence in teaching, and in Bard’s mission as a private college in the public interest. Now entering its third decade, the Bard Early College network enrolls over 3,300 young people in campuses in Queens, Manhattan, the Bronx, Brooklyn, and Hudson, New York; Newark, New Jersey; New Orleans, Louisiana; Cleveland, Ohio; Baltimore, Maryland; and Washington, D.C. Expertise in the formal teaching of writing is also desirable. Candidates with expertise in history of the Americas and/or American studies may be considered for dual appointments in English and History. Candidates will teach American Literature at the high school and college levels; candidates will teach courses in their fields of specialization, as well as interdisciplinary courses in the Humanities. Successful applicants will be innovative teachers, skilled in leading interactive, seminar style classes, and engaging students from widely diverse backgrounds. jobs.description: Employer: Cambridge Health Alliance Expires: 08/27/2026 Cambridge Health Alliance (CHA) is a vibrant, innovative health system dedicated to providing essential services to all members of the community. With almost 140,000 patients in Cambridge, Somerville, and Boston’s Metro North region, CHA is a local provider of choice for primary care, specialty care, emergency services, hospital care, maternity care and behavioral health. CHA opened an inpatient center for youth with acute behavioral health needs. Located in Somerville, the beautiful facility offers care for children, adolescents, and children with acute neurodevelopmental challenges. The Center for Inpatient Child & Adolescent Psychiatry at Somerville provides a transformative continuum of patient and family-centered care for diverse youth with mental health needs. jobs.description: Employer: Dallas Football Officials Association Expires: 08/27/2026 Join – DFOA This is an on-site seasonal officiating position with the Dallas Football Officials Association (www.DFOA.com) starting in August through November of 2026 in the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex. You will be responsible for officiating middle and high schools that the DFOA serves in the DFW metroplex. You will be paid from the collection of fees billed to the schools you officiate. This is a great opportunity for anyone living or moving to the DFW metroplex to build a career officiating football and earn extra money!This seasonal officiating position is available every year from August to November.Games start around 5:00 PM and end 9:00 PM Monday through Friday. You can expect 1-2 games Monday - Thursday your first year of officiating. You can pick your own schedule and days you are available within our scheduling application Reftown. Follow the below link to see the pay per game:Officials Fee Schedule — University Interscholastic League (UIL) AboutThe Dallas Football Officials Association (DFOA) is one of the largest and premier chapters of football officials in Texas and the United States. With approximately 700 members who officiate football not only in the Dallas & Ft. Worth surrounding areas but also throughout the State of Texas. The DFOA is comprised of new officials to experienced veterans with 50+ years of service and many in-between. We are a chapter in the Texas Association of Sport Officials (TASO), which is the UIL recognized officiating organization providing officials for middle and high school football contests throughout the state of Texas. TASO works directly with the University Interscholastic League (UIL), the governing body of public schools in Texas, as well as the Texas Association of Private and Parochial Schools (TAPPS), the largest organization of private schools in Texas to provide experienced and trained officials for their football contests. Each year, the DFOA makes agreements with local schools and districts to provide football officials for their varsity and sub-varsity football games. Our chapter typically has 6,000+ officiating game assignments starting with scrimmages then week one of the season and all the way to through the UIL & TAPPS Championship games at the end of the season. New Member Registration:In order to become an Official in the Dallas Football Officials Association (DFOA) you must join the Texas Association of Sports Officials (TASO) and our chapter, DFOA. You will be required to pay a total of $125 for your first season. There are 2 steps you must complete for the membership process. 1) First join TASO: Go to: www.taso.org then click on “Apply” button in the New Applicants section on the TASO home page. This step will require online payment of $50. 2) Next, join DFOA, Go to https://www.dfoa.com/join/ to register. This step will require online payment of $75. 3) Register in Reftown, which is the online tool the DFOA uses to schedule you to officiate football games. To register go to https://reftown.com/registration.asp. There is no charge for this registration. Your membership allows you the opportunity to work DFOA assigned games. Each new member official will also receive an NCAA rule book. Additionally, new member officials will be granted access to the members section of the TASO website where you will find additional useful information. Attention: Military Veterans. There is an organization called Battlefields-to-Ballfields that has partnered with TASO to offer a scholarship that reimburses a member’s initial uniform and 3 years of dues. If you have ever served in the US Military, we highly encourage you to visit this great organizations website to take advantage of this wonderful benefit. We also thank you for your service. Our chapter has numerous officials who are also Veterans as well. MeetingsNew member training sessions are provided each season. These meetings are typically scheduled from 6:30 PM to 8:00PM on Monday evenings and will start in June of each year and go up until the season starts. The meetings are designed for the benefit of the officials and are an invaluable source of education and training at all levels. Some of these meeting dates may actually be on-field training sessions for new members. The location and time of the meetings will be posted on the DFOA website (www.dfoa.com) so please check the website regularly to get the latest information. Game FeesSub varsity game fees are determined by the UIL. Most schools will have you fill out a pay sheet and a W-9 form and then mail you a check within 2-3 weeks or they may use Arbiter pay where you can get paid typically in 1 week. Sub-varsity game fees range from $50-$65 per game plus a minimum of $20 for travel pay based on distance of the game site from the chapter center point. Varsity games range from $115 minimum per game and goes up based on gate receipts and distance of the game site from the chapter center point. This is just a general range and could vary depending on each school district. Each school district may require a completed W-9 form each year. Once you have completed a W-9 for a specific school district the next time you officiate a game in that district you do not need to put your Social Security number on their game site paperwork-just indicate “ON-FILE”. It is only necessary to provide your Social Security number the first time you officiate in that district. Start your officiating career at www.DFOA.com by going to the Join tab

jobs.title: Youth Soccer Aide at The Salvation Army - San Angelo TX
jobs.description: Employer: The Salvation Army - San Angelo TX Expires: 08/27/2026 We are seeking a passionate, energetic soccer lover to inspire and teach youth players. If you enjoy helping kids learn, improve, and have fun on the field, this is a great fit. This is a part-time Aide role. Expectations: Plan/teach and lead engaging soccer practices for youth age groups (5–12 years old).Teach fundamental skills (dribbling, passing, shooting, defending) and introduce game concepts in an age-appropriate way.Create a positive, inclusive, and safe training environment; emphasize teamwork, sportsmanship, and enjoyment of the game.Organize and run small-sided games and drills; provide clear demonstrations and feedback.Ensure all activities comply with safety guidelines; perform basic first aid if necessary and report injuries appropriately.Qualifications:Genuine passion for soccer and a love of teaching kids.Prior coaching or youth basketball/soccer experience is a plus; willingness to learn and adapt.Strong communication and interpersonal skills; patient, encouraging, and fun-loving demeanor.Ability to motivate kids, manage groups, and keep practices organized.Basic knowledge of soccer tactics suitable for youth players; ability to explain concepts simply.First Aid/CPR certification (or willingness to obtain).Flexible availability for weekday evenings and some weekend hours.

jobs.description: Employer: Kumon Math and Reading Center of Mequon Expires: 08/27/2026 As a Part Time Kumon Assistant, your daily responsibilities usually include preparing student worksheets, grading assignments, providing guidance during study sessions, and assisting with administrative tasks like maintaining records. You’ll work closely with both students and the instructor, helping to foster a supportive learning environment. Assisting students one-on-one or in small groups, you play an important role in encouraging independent study habits and reinforcing the Kumon method.
